title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-03-30
content:
Summary:
Quick roundup for the week of 2026-03-24 -> 2026-03-30. Focus areas: GPU fleet health, region capacity, short-term buying plan for Q2, and follow-ups from last week's outage. This is a working doc — please add comments inline or drop notes in #infra-weekly.

Highlights:
- Fleet availability recovered to target after partial outage on 3/25 (see Incident section).
- Baseline GPU utilization (hosted + dedicated) averaged 68% across all pools; peak sustained for 6 hours at 92% in us-west1 during model benchmark runs.
- We validated the first pass of the Q2 purchase quote (NVIDIA H120 equivalent on-prem rack offer) and identified a shortfall of ~420 vGPU-equivalents in eu-west1.
- Autoscaler tuning rolled out to prod pools (batching/slot sizing) reduced small-request latency by ~15% and improved throughput headroom.

GPU Fleet Status (by pool):
- us-west1-primary (A100/NH): healthy. 95% of machines online. Rolling kernel patch completed 3/28 with no regressions. Avg util 62%.
- us-east1-burst (H100 & T4 mix): intermittent throttling during 3/25 outage window; currently stable. Avg util 73%.
- eu-west1-new (H120 test cluster): still in validation. Perf variance on long-context LLMs (seq len > 4k). Need follow-up with runtime team (tagged below). Avg util 44% (low because we held back traffic).
- ap-southeast1-smoke (T4/GPU-small): serving internal evals only; capacity ok for now, but we should revisit before APAC customer ramp in May.

Capacity Planning & Regions:
- Current immediate headroom across hosted fleets: ~18% aggregate (measured as idle vGPU-equivalents). This is borderline for forecasted marketing-run spikes and model eval campaigns planned for mid-April.
- eu-west1 shortfall: forecast demand vs committed capacity indicates we need +420 vGPU-equivalents by 2026-04-21 to keep p95 latency targets under current routing policy without frequent fallbacks. (See JIRA-INF-4321 for calculator sheet).
- Suggested mitigations (short-term):
  1) Re-route non-critical evaluation traffic from eu-west1 to us-west1 during business hours (policy change, low-impact).
  2) Enable burst credits for Dedicated customers where possible (billing + ops coordination).
  3) Expedite procurement for one H120 rack in eu-west1 (procurement + legal hold-ups noted; Priya to follow).
- Longer-term: Q3 plan to homogenize instance types across eu regions to simplify scheduler and capacity packing (will reduce fragmentation).

Incident review — Partial Fleet Outage (2026-03-25 02:10–03:40 UTC):
- Impact: brief 90–120 minute window where autoscaler mis-evaluated node health during a kernel update rollout leading to ~12% increased tail latency for hosted text-gen endpoints in us-east1 and eu-west1. No data loss. Dedicated customers experienced elevated queueing for ~45 minutes.
- Root cause: kernel rollout combined with a DNS cache TTL mismatch in the autoscaler health-check path.
- Mitigation completed: reverted kernel on affected nodes, increased health-check TTL safety margin, paused phased rollout.
- Action items:
  - INF-OPS: add pre-rollout chaos check (simulate health-check flapping) into blue/green automation — owner: Tom (ETA 2026-04-06).
  - SRE: add one-minute grace to autoscaler before evicting nodes during concurrent update events — owner: Ian (ETA 2026-04-02).
  - Infra: review DNS caching config across all pools and ensure consistent TTLs — owner: Aisha (ETA 2026-04-05).

Optimization and cost controls:
- Autoscaler tuning (slot sizing) decreased small-request cpu/gpu churn — estimated monthly savings $28k across hosted fleet if changes remain stable. Tracking in JIRA-OPS-987.
- Batching improvements reduced median token cost by ~8% for chat workloads during peak. Need to monitor for edge-case latency regressions.

Testing & Validation:
- eu-west1 H120 long-context regression: found slightly higher VRAM fragmentation on sequences >4k; runtime team to try alternative allocator flags in next canary (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/214).
- Load test schedule: 2026-04-08 run planned to validate updated autoscaler and allocator flags (owners: Priya + runtime team).

Open questions / To decide:
- Buy vs borrow: Do we purchase an extra rack for eu-west1 now (capex + lead time) or temporarily increase cross-region routing? Cost + SLA trade-offs need leadership input. (Finance + Product sync required).
- Dedicated burst pricing: can we offer temporary burst credits without breaking current pricing constructs? (product + finance).

Meeting notes / standups this week:
- 3/26 Infra sync: covered outage RCA, autoscaler changes, and Q2 buys. Notes: small consensus to prioritize short-term re-routing while procurement clears.
- 3/27 Capacity planning tabletop with Sales: Sales requested guaranteed eu capacity for two upcoming enterprise deals (expected May). We scoped a 60-day provisional plan — sales to confirm commitment.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Priya: chase procurement quote and vendor lead time for H120-equivalent rack in eu-west1 — ETA 2026-04-02.
- Tom: implement rollout pre-checks in deployment pipeline & add chaos simulation tests — ETA 2026-04-06.
- Ian: autoscaler grace-period change + rollout plan — ETA 2026-04-02.
- Aisha: DNS TTL audit across pools and update runbook — ETA 2026-04-05.
- Runtime team: canary of allocator flags in eu-west1 (PR #214) and post-mortem perf comparison — ETA 2026-04-08 (post-load test).

Notes / context snippets (scratch):
- Slack thread: #infra-gpu "kernel patch caused health-check flapping" (see linked_artifacts slack id).
- Confluence plan link: GPU Fleet Capacity Plan Q2 2026 (linked above).
- TODO: Draft customer-facing note for dedicated customers affected by 3/25 elevated queueing — coordinate with CS and legal.

Next sync: Mon 2026-04-06 (infra weekly). Add extra 30m buffer for procurement review.

Document history / edits:
- 2026-03-30 Aisha Patel: initial draft (this file).
- 2026-03-30 comments expected from Tom + Priya + Ian.

End of update.
